decisions.reason: After two years without website presence, this low-prominence but related component likely appears to have fallen short of aspirations, so management would reallocate capacity to stronger core fittings work.

Although no longer visible online, this bracket is closely tied to existing fabrication jobs and can be carried at low incremental cost, so management would likely keep it unless clearer evidence of shortfall emerges.
This support bracket remains a natural extension of the core offer and shared resources create slack for continued supply despite uncertain standalone performance.

As a more distant diversification into street furniture, the waste bin would be harder to justify against aspiration levels when core infrastructure products offer a better use of fabrication and coating resources.

Even with several models, this waste-bin-with-ashtray line sits outside the main pipeline business and, absent clear success signals, management would likely trim it in favor of core products and nearer developments.

Standalone outdoor ashtrays are the most peripheral to the firm's established offer, so uncertain results would likely trigger problemistic search and redeployment back to core municipal-infrastructure work.
